title: Syria to Launch Vaccination Drive Against Polio
desc: Syria's health ministry is preparing a vast vaccination campaign, with UN backing, to protect children in the eastern province of Deir Ezzor against polio, following the detection of three cases. Polio, which mainly affects children under five, is an infectious disease. One in 200 infections leads to irreversible paralysis, and among those paralyzed, five to 10 percent die. Thanks to immunization efforts, the disease has mostly been eradicated globally.

title: Dynamic visualization of cell adhesion molecule interactions using reversible split-HaloTag labeling in living cells
desc: Critical for diverse cellular functions, cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) interact to transduce information from the external environment to drive coordinated intracellular responses. However, direct visualization of CAM interactions in living cells and organisms remains a major challenge. Recent developments in split-HaloTag technology present a promising strategy for chemical labeling of protein–protein interactions. Here, we apply this method to dynamically monitor CAM interactions in living HEK293T cells using split-HaloTag-CAM fusion proteins. With high specificity, we visualized trans-cellular interactions between known adhesion pairs natively found in neuronal and immunological synapses. To expand the system’s versatility, we adapted a modified split-HaloTag component (cpHaloΔN272H) that enables reversible dye exchange and facilitates rapid time-lapse imaging of CAM interactions. Leveraging fluorogenic HaloTag dyes, split-HaloTag-CAMs measured the real-time disassembly and reassembly of Ca2+-dependent CAM junctions in live cells. These tools enabled imaging long-term changes in surface contacts mediated by CAM binding, thus providing a robust platform for dissecting the spatiotemporal dynamics of CAM interactions in cellular and organismal contexts.
